questions.title: Activity Selection Peak
questions.description:
A conference hosts activities with (start, end) times given in arbitrary order. The classic greedy: sort by END time, take the first activity, then take every activity that starts at or after the last accepted one ended — touching activities (start == previous end) are compatible. Report the maximum number of activities one person can attend. No imports or heapq — pure Python only (sort with sorted).

The scaffolding (input reading and pair building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def max_activities(intervals):

intervals is a list of (start, end) pairs in input order. Sort with sorted by end time, sweep greedily, and return the maximum compatible count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the activity count.
Next n lines: start end.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of activities.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= start < end <= 1000000

questions.title: After One Bubble Pass
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def after_one_bubble_pass(values):

Perform exactly ONE full bubble-sort pass over values (compare every adjacent pair left to right, swapping when the left is larger) and return the list state after that single pass.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the list after one bubble pass, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200
-1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def after_one_bubble_pass(values):
    a = values[:]
    for j in range(len(a) - 1):
        if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
            a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
    return a


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = after_one_bubble_pass(values)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

A DJ shuffles two playlists strictly alternately (track from list A, track from list B, ...); when one list runs out, the leftovers of the other are appended. The zip builtin is banned.

    def interleave(a, b):

Input Format:

Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: m.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def interleave(a, b):
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(a) or i < len(b):
        if i < len(a):
            out.append(a[i])
        if i < len(b):
            out.append(b[i])
        i += 1
    return out


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
m = int(data[1 + n])
b = list(map(int, data[2 + n:2 + n + m]))
print(" ".join(map(str, interleave(a, b))))

questions.title: Append to the Audit Chain
questions.description:
An audit trail appends each new event at the TAIL of a doubly linked chain; the tail's next and the new node's prev must both be wired.

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def insert_back(head, x):

head is the head Node of the audit chain. Allocate Node(x), link it after the current tail (fix the tail's next and the new node's prev) and return the head. The harness prints the chain forward AND backward to verify both directions.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of events.
Line 2: n integers — the event codes in chain order.
Line 3: the new event code x.

Output Format:
Line 1: the chain forward, space-separated.
Line 2: the chain backward, space-separated.
(Both lines are printed by the harness.)

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value, x <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def insert_back(head, x):
    node = Node(x)
    if head is None:
        return node
    tail = head
    while tail.next is not None:
        tail = tail.next
    tail.next = node
    node.prev = tail
    return head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    x = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    head = insert_back(head, x)
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_forward(head))))
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_backward(head))))


main()

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def binary_search(values, x):
    lo, hi = 0, len(values) - 1
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if values[mid] == x:
            return mid
        if values[mid] < x:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    return -1


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
x = int(data[1 + n])
print(binary_search(values, x))

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def probe_count(values, x):

Run the standard binary search with mid = (lo + hi) // 2 and count how many times a middle element is examined until x is found. x is always present, so the loop ends on a match.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers in ascending order.
Line 3: the target x (always present).

Output Format:
One line with the number of probes.

Constraints:

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def probe_count(values, x):
    lo, hi = 0, len(values) - 1
    probes = 0
    while lo <= hi:
        probes += 1
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if values[mid] == x:
            break
        if values[mid] < x:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    return probes


data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
x = int(data[1 + n])
print(probe_count(values, x))

questions.title: Bubble After k Passes
questions.description:
A sorting visualiser snapshots the array between rounds. Reproduce exactly what the board shows after k bubble passes — no shortcuts to the final result.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def bubble_after_k_passes(values, k):

Perform exactly k full bubble passes (each pass compares every adjacent pair left to right and swaps out-of-order neighbours) and return the list state after pass k.

Input Format:

import sys


def bubble_after_k_passes(values, k):
    a = values[:]
    n = len(a)
    for _ in range(k):
        for j in range(n - 1):
            if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
                a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
    return a


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    k = int(data[1 + n])
    result = bubble_after_k_passes(values, k)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

import sys


def bubble_swaps(values):
    a = values[:]
    n = len(a)
    swaps = 0
    for i in range(n - 1):
        for j in range(n - 1 - i):
            if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
                a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
                swaps += 1
    return swaps


def main():

questions.title: Bubble Swaps vs Insertion Shifts
questions.description:
A performance lab compares the basic sorts on identical data: how many adjacent swaps does bubble make, and how many shifts does insertion need? Report both work counters side by side.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def bubble_vs_insertion(values):

Return the tuple (bubble_swaps, insertion_shifts): the total adjacent swaps bubble sort performs on a copy of values, and the total shifts insertion sort performs on another copy.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the two counters, space-separated: bubble swaps, then insertion shifts.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 200
-1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def bubble_vs_insertion(values):
    a = values[:]
    n = len(a)
    swaps = 0
    for i in range(n - 1):
        for j in range(n - 1 - i):
            if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
                a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
                swaps += 1
    b = values[:]
    shifts = 0
    for i in range(1, len(b)):
        key = b[i]
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and b[j] > key:
            b[j + 1] = b[j]
            shifts += 1
            j -= 1
        b[j + 1] = key
    return swaps, shifts


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = bubble_vs_insertion(values)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

questions.title: Build Order Smallest First
questions.description:
A build server must schedule tasks with dependencies. Kahn's algorithm repeatedly takes any task whose in-degree dropped to 0 — and the pipeline policy breaks ties by the SMALLEST task index to keep builds reproducible. Output the full order. The graph is guaranteed acyclic; no imports or heapq — scan for the smallest ready index each round.

The program scaffolding (input reading and adjacency building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def topo_order(adj):

adj is the dependency adjacency dict keyed 0..V-1 (edge u -> v means u before v). Track an indeg map, repeatedly pick the smallest-index vertex with indeg 0, append it to the order and decrement its targets' in-degrees. Return the topological order list; the harness prints it space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E — task count and dependency count.

import sys


class Node:

def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None

def build_singly(values):

    tail = None

    while node is not None:

def dll_backward(head):

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def dll_delete_at(head, pos):
    node = head
    i = 0
    while i < pos:
        node = node.next
        i += 1
    if node.prev is not None:
        node.prev.next = node.next
    else:
        head = node.next
    if node.next is not None:
        node.next.prev = node.prev
    return head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    pos = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    head = dll_delete_at(head, pos)
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_forward(head))))
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_backward(head))))


main()

CANONICAL_COINS = [1000, 500, 100, 50, 20, 10, 5, 2, 1]


def min_coins(amount, coins):

    for c in coins:

    return count

import sys


def lomuto_swaps(values):
    a = values[:]

A photo-album fixer counts how out-of-order a big sequence is. The brute-force double loop is too slow for the archive, so count inversions DURING the merges of merge sort.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def inversion_count(values):

Count pairs i < j with values[i] > values[j] using merge sort: while merging two sorted halves, every time an element of the right half goes first, it is smaller than all remaining left-half elements — add that many inversions at once. Return the total.

Input Format:

Line 2: n integers.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def inversion_count(values):
    def sort_count(arr):
        if len(arr) <= 1:
            return arr[:], 0
        mid = len(arr) // 2
        left, li = sort_count(arr[:mid])
        right, ri = sort_count(arr[mid:])
        merged = []
        inv = li + ri
        i = j = 0
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                j += 1
                inv += len(left) - i
        while i < len(left):
            merged.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        while j < len(right):
            merged.append(right[j])
            j += 1
        return merged, inv

    return sort_count(values)[1]


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = inversion_count(values)
    print(result)


main()

questions.title: Crate Unload Order
questions.description:
A yard crane unloads crates stacked as a binary tree: the root crate always comes off first, then the whole left stack, then the whole right stack — exactly a preorder walk.

The program scaffolding (input reading, TNode class and tree building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def preorder(root, out):

root is the root TNode of the crate tree and out is the unload list you must fill with the crate codes in preorder. The harness prints the filled list.

The tree has at least one node.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


class TNode:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.val = v
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def build_tree(tokens):
    it = iter(tokens)
    first = next(it, -1)
    if first == -1:
        return None
    root = TNode(first)
    q = [root]
    for node in q:
        l = next(it, -1)
        if l != -1:
            node.left = TNode(l)
            q.append(node.left)
        r = next(it, -1)
        if r != -1:
            node.right = TNode(r)
            q.append(node.right)
    return root


def preorder(root, out):
    if root is None:
        return
    out.append(root.val)
    preorder(root.left, out)
    preorder(root.right, out)


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    root = build_tree(list(map(int, lines[1].split())))
    out = []
    preorder(root, out)
    print(' '.join(map(str, out)))


main()

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def build_chain_with_cycle(values, pos):
    head = build_chain(values)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        steps = pos
        while steps > 0:
            target = target.next
            steps -= 1
        tail.next = target
    return head

def has_cycle(head):
    slow = head
    fast = head
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        if slow is fast:
            return True
    return False


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    pos = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_chain_with_cycle(values, pos)
    print(has_cycle(head))


main()

import sys


def count_arrangements(letters):
    if not letters:

    seen = []

    i = 0

            rest = letters[:i] + letters[i + 1:]
            total += count_arrangements(rest)
        i += 1
    return total

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def dll_length(head):
    count = 0
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    return count


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    head = build_dll_chain(values)

main()

def longest_window(nums, limit):
    best = 0
    total = 0
    left = 0
    for right in range(len(nums)):

            total -= nums[left]
            left += 1
        if right - left + 1 > best:

import sys


def copy_count(n):
    capacity = 1
    size = 0

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def find_index(head, x):
    idx = 0
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        if node.value == x:
            return idx
        idx += 1
        node = node.next
    return -1

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def reverse_dll(head):

head is the head Node of a doubly linked chain. Reverse the chain by swapping each node's prev and next while walking it (after the swap, advance through node.prev!) and return the new head (the old tail). The harness prints the chain forward AND backward to verify both directions.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def reverse_dll(head):
    node = head
    new_head = head
    while node is not None:
        node.prev, node.next = node.next, node.prev
        new_head = node
        node = node.prev
    return new_head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    head = reverse_dll(head)
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_forward(head))))
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_backward(head))))


main()

import sys


def bubble_trace(values):
    a = values[:]
    n = len(a)
    states = []
    swapped = True
    while swapped:
        swapped = False
        for j in range(n - 1):
            if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
                a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
                swapped = True
        states.append(a[:])
    return states


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    states = bubble_trace(values)
    lines = []

    print('\n'.join(lines))

s = input()


def longest_palindrome(s):
    n = len(s)
    best_start = 0
    best_len = 1
    for center in range(n):
        left = center
        right = center
        while left >= 0 and right < n and s[left] == s[right]:
            left -= 1
            right += 1
        if right - left - 1 > best_len:
            best_len = right - left - 1
            best_start = left + 1
        left = center
        right = center + 1
        while left >= 0 and right < n and s[left] == s[right]:
            left -= 1
            right += 1
        if right - left - 1 > best_len:
            best_len = right - left - 1
            best_start = left + 1
    return s[best_start:best_start + best_len]


print(longest_palindrome(s))

from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def survivor(names, p):
    q = deque(names)
    while len(q) > 1:
        for _ in range(p - 1):
            q.append(q.popleft())
        q.popleft()
    return q[0]


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    p = int(lines[0].split()[1])
    names = lines[1].split()
    print(survivor(names, p))


main()

questions.sourcecode:
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


class TNode:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.val = v
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def build_tree(tokens):
    it = iter(tokens)
    first = next(it, -1)
    if first == -1:
        return None
    root = TNode(first)
    q = [root]
    for node in q:
        l = next(it, -1)
        if l != -1:
            node.left = TNode(l)
            q.append(node.left)
        r = next(it, -1)
        if r != -1:
            node.right = TNode(r)
            q.append(node.right)
    return root


def inorder(root, out):
    if root is None:
        return
    inorder(root.left, out)
    out.append(root.val)
    inorder(root.right, out)


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    root = build_tree(list(map(int, lines[1].split())))
    out = []
    inorder(root, out)
    print(' '.join(map(str, out)))


main()

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def insert_in_order(head, x):
    node = Node(x)
    if head is None or x < head.value:
        node.next = head
        return node
    prev = head
    while prev.next is not None and prev.next.value <= x:
        prev = prev.next
    node.next = prev.next
    prev.next = node
    return head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    x = int(data[1 + n])

    head = insert_in_order(head, x)
    print(' '.join(map(str, chain_values(head))))

head is the head Node of an ascending doubly chain. Allocate Node(x), insert it keeping the chain ascending (head case included) and return the (possibly new) head. The harness prints the chain forward AND backward to verify both directions.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def dll_insert_ascending(head, x):
    node = Node(x)
    if head is None or x < head.value:
        node.next = head
        if head is not None:
            head.prev = node
        return node
    prev = head
    while prev.next is not None and prev.next.value <= x:
        prev = prev.next
    node.next = prev.next
    node.prev = prev
    if prev.next is not None:
        prev.next.prev = node
    prev.next = node
    return head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    x = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    head = dll_insert_ascending(head, x)
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_forward(head))))
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_backward(head))))


main()

    parts = sorted(ropes)
    total = 0

        a = parts.pop(0)
        b = parts.pop(0)

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def circular_insert_back(head, x):
    node = Node(x)
    tail = head
    while tail.next is not head:
        tail = tail.next
    tail.next = node
    node.next = head
    return head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    x = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_circle(values)
    head = circular_insert_back(head, x)
    print(' '.join(map(str, circle_lap(head))))


main()

import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


class TNode:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.val = v
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def build_tree(tokens):
    it = iter(tokens)
    first = next(it, -1)
    if first == -1:
        return None
    root = TNode(first)
    q = [root]
    for node in q:
        l = next(it, -1)
        if l != -1:
            node.left = TNode(l)
            q.append(node.left)
        r = next(it, -1)
        if r != -1:
            node.right = TNode(r)
            q.append(node.right)
    return root


def inorder_values(root):
    out = []

    def walk(node):
        if node is None:
            return
        walk(node.left)
        out.append(node.val)
        walk(node.right)

    walk(root)
    return out


def kth_smallest(root, k):
    stack = []
    node = root
    while stack or node is not None:
        while node is not None:
            stack.append(node)
            node = node.left
        node = stack.pop()
        k -= 1
        if k == 0:
            return node.val
        node = node.right
    return -1


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    root = build_tree(list(map(int, lines[1].split())))
    k = int(lines[2])
    print(kth_smallest(root, k))


main()

import sys


def leaderboard(pairs):
    a = pairs[:]

    for i in range(n):

    def find_from_tail(tail, x):

tail is the TAIL Node of a doubly linked chain and x is the queried code. Return the 0-based index counting FROM the tail (tail itself is 0), or -1 when x is not in the chain.

Input Format:

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def find_from_tail(tail, x):
    node = tail
    idx = 0
    while node is not None:
        if node.value == x:
            return idx
        node = node.prev
        idx += 1
    return -1


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    x = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    print(find_from_tail(tail, x))


main()

def read_pairs(n):

        a, b = map(int, input().split())

def max_units(box_types, truck_size):
    order = sorted(box_types, key=lambda b: b[1], reverse=True)

    space = truck_size

import sys


def lomuto_index(values):
    a = values[:]
    n = len(a)
    pivot = a[n - 1]
    i = -1
    for j in range(n - 1):
        if a[j] <= pivot:
            i += 1
            a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
    a[i + 1], a[n - 1] = a[n - 1], a[i + 1]
    return i + 1


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()

import sys


def median_two(a, b):
    need = (len(a) + len(b)) // 2
    i = j = 0
    last = 0
    while i + j <= need:
        if i < len(a) and (j >= len(b) or a[i] <= b[j]):
            last = a[i]
            i += 1
        else:
            last = b[j]
            j += 1
    return last

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):

        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:

        else:

questions.description:
A rail terminus needs enough platforms so no train waits: train i arrives at arrivals[i] and leaves at departures[i]. A train arriving exactly when another departs CANNOT reuse that platform — equal times count as overlapping. Sort both time lists independently and sweep with two pointers, tracking how many trains sit in the station simultaneously. Report the platform minimum. The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

def min_platforms(arrivals, departures):
    arrivals = sorted(arrivals)
    departures = sorted(departures)
    best = 1
    i = 0
    n = len(arrivals)
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j < n and arrivals[j] == arrivals[i]:
            j += 1
        if j - i > best:
            best = j - i
        i = j
    return best


def main():
    n = int(input())
    arrivals = list(map(int, input().split()))
    departures = list(map(int, input().split()))
    print(min_platforms(arrivals, departures))


main()

A browser history chain stores pages in a doubly linked chain; the UI highlights a page and shows its previous and next page. Read both directions through the node's prev and next pointers.

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def neighbours(head, i):
    node = head
    k = 0
    while k < i:
        node = node.next
        k += 1
    left = node.prev.value if node.prev is not None else -1
    right = node.next.value if node.next is not None else -1
    return [left, node.value, right]


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    i = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    result = neighbours(head, i)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and circular chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def circular_values(head):

head is the head Node of a CIRCULAR singly chain. Return the list of values seen during exactly one lap around the circle, starting at head and stopping when you return to it.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of nodes.
Line 2: n integers — the node values in circle order.

Output Format:
One line with the values of one lap, space-separated (printed by the harness).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def circular_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    out.append(node.value)
    node = node.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    head = build_circle(values)
    result = circular_values(head)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

questions.description:
A quiz app groups scores around the last recorded score before recursing: everything <= the pivot drifts left, everything else stays right. Show the array after the pass.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def partition_scores(scores):

Run one Lomuto partition on a copy of scores with the LAST element as pivot and the <= convention, and return the array as it looks after the pass.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of scores.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the partitioned array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500
0 <= score <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def partition_scores(scores):
    a = scores[:]
    n = len(a)
    pivot = a[n - 1]
    i = -1
    for j in range(n - 1):
        if a[j] <= pivot:
            i += 1
            a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
    a[i + 1], a[n - 1] = a[n - 1], a[i + 1]
    return a


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = partition_scores(values)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

questions.title: Passes Until Bubble Settles
questions.description:
A classroom exercise asks: how many bubble passes does THIS data need before a pass completes with no swaps? Count them by simulating the sort with early exit.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def passes_until_settled(values):

Simulate bubble sort with early exit and return the number of full passes performed, counting the final swap-free pass (an already-sorted list needs exactly 1).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the number of passes until the list settles.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100
-1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def passes_until_settled(values):
    a = values[:]
    n = len(a)
    passes = 0
    swapped = True
    while swapped:
        swapped = False
        passes += 1
        for j in range(n - 1):
            if a[j] > a[j + 1]:
                a[j], a[j + 1] = a[j + 1], a[j]
                swapped = True
    return passes


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = passes_until_settled(values)
    print(result)


main()

questions.title: Peak Element Index
questions.description:
A load monitor reads a sequence where the traffic rises then falls somewhere (no two neighbours are equal). Report the peak using the standard converging binary search.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def peak_index(values):

A peak is an element strictly greater than its neighbours (boundary elements only need to beat their single neighbour). Run exactly this binary search and return the index it converges to: lo = 0, hi = n-1; while lo < hi: mid = (lo + hi) // 2; if values[mid] < values[mid + 1]: lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid; return lo. No two adjacent values are equal, so this always lands on a valid peak.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values (n >= 2).
Line 2: n integers, no two adjacent values equal.

Output Format:
One line with the peak index.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000

import sys


def peak_index(values):
    lo, hi = 0, len(values) - 1
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if values[mid] < values[mid + 1]:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid
    return lo


data = sys.stdin.read().split()

from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def start_station(petrol, dist):
    total = 0
    curr = 0
    start = 0
    for i in range(len(petrol)):
        d = petrol[i] - dist[i]
        total += d
        curr += d
        if curr < 0:
            start = i + 1
            curr = 0
    return start if total >= 0 else -1


def main():

    petrol = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    dist = list(map(int, lines[2].split()))
    print(start_station(petrol, dist))

questions.description:
A radar console sorts contact points (x, y) by distance from the origin; ties in distance are broken by smaller x, then by smaller y.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def points_by_distance(points):

points is a list of (x, y) tuples. Sort them by x*x + y*y ascending, breaking ties by x ascending and then y ascending, with a manual sort and compound comparison. Return the sorted list of tuples.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of points.
Lines 2..n+1: two integers per point: x and y.

Output Format:
n lines, one per point in sorted order: x and y space-separated.

Constraints:

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def points_by_distance(points):
    a = points[:]
    n = len(a)
    for i in range(n):
        m = i
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            kj = (a[j][0] * a[j][0] + a[j][1] * a[j][1], a[j][0], a[j][1])
            km = (a[m][0] * a[m][0] + a[m][1] * a[m][1], a[m][0], a[m][1])
            if kj < km:
                m = j
        a[i], a[m] = a[m], a[i]
    return a


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    points = []
    idx = 1
    for _ in range(n):
        points.append((int(data[idx]), int(data[idx + 1])))
        idx += 2
    result = points_by_distance(points)
    out = []
    for x, y in result:
        out.append(str(x) + ' ' + str(y))
    print('\n'.join(out))


main()

questions.description:
The program scaffolding (input reading, TNode class and tree building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def postorder(root, out):

root is the root TNode of a binary tree and out is a list you must fill with the node values in POSTORDER (left subtree, then right subtree, then root). The harness prints the filled list.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values in the level-order serialization.
Line 2: n integers — the tree in level order (-1 marks a missing child).

Output Format:

The tree has at least one node.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


class TNode:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.val = v
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def build_tree(tokens):
    it = iter(tokens)
    first = next(it, -1)
    if first == -1:
        return None
    root = TNode(first)
    q = [root]
    for node in q:
        l = next(it, -1)
        if l != -1:
            node.left = TNode(l)
            q.append(node.left)
        r = next(it, -1)
        if r != -1:
            node.right = TNode(r)
            q.append(node.right)
    return root


def postorder(root, out):
    if root is None:
        return
    postorder(root.left, out)
    postorder(root.right, out)

The program scaffolding (input reading, TNode class and tree building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def preorder(root, out):

root is the root TNode of a binary tree (each node has val, left, right) and out is a list you must fill with the node values in PREORDER (root first, then the left subtree, then the right subtree). The harness prints the filled list.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


class TNode:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.val = v
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def build_tree(tokens):
    it = iter(tokens)
    first = next(it, -1)
    if first == -1:
        return None
    root = TNode(first)
    q = [root]
    for node in q:
        l = next(it, -1)
        if l != -1:
            node.left = TNode(l)
            q.append(node.left)
        r = next(it, -1)
        if r != -1:
            node.right = TNode(r)
            q.append(node.right)
    return root


def preorder(root, out):
    if root is None:
        return
    out.append(root.val)
    preorder(root.left, out)
    preorder(root.right, out)


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    root = build_tree(list(map(int, lines[1].split())))
    out = []
    preorder(root, out)
    print(' '.join(map(str, out)))


main()

A service kiosk keeps waiting tickets on a doubly linked chain; an emergency ticket must be inserted at the FRONT with both pointer directions fixed.

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

head is the head Node of the ticket chain. Allocate Node(x), place it before the current head (set its next, fix the old head's prev) and return the new head. The harness prints the chain forward AND backward to verify both directions.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def insert_front(head, x):
    node = Node(x)
    node.next = head
    if head is not None:
        head.prev = node
    return node


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    x = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    head = insert_front(head, x)
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_forward(head))))
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_backward(head))))


main()

questions.title: Quickselect the Kth Smallest
questions.description:
A metrics service answers kth-smallest queries on live percentiles without sorting everything: quickselect partitions around the last element and recurses into one side only. Values are distinct.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def quickselect_kth(values, k):

values holds DISTINCT integers. Return the k-th smallest value (1-indexed) using iterative quickselect: repeatedly Lomuto-partition (last-element pivot, <=) around a shrinking [lo, hi] window until the pivot lands on index k-1.

Input Format:

Line 2: n distinct integers.
Line 3: k (1 <= k <= n).

Output Format:

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def quickselect_kth(values, k):
    a = values[:]
    lo, hi = 0, len(a) - 1
    target = k - 1
    while True:
        pivot = a[hi]
        i = lo - 1
        for j in range(lo, hi):
            if a[j] <= pivot:
                i += 1
                a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
        a[i + 1], a[hi] = a[hi], a[i + 1]
        p = i + 1
        if p == target:
            return a[p]
        if p < target:
            lo = p + 1
        else:
            hi = p - 1


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    k = int(data[1 + n])
    print(quickselect_kth(values, k))


main()

questions.title: Quicksort the List
questions.description:
The final boss of the week: full quicksort by hand. Partition around the last element, recurse on both sides — no builtin sorting.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def quicksort_list(values):

Sort a copy of values ascending with recursive quicksort: write a partition(...) helper (Lomuto, last-element pivot, <=) and recurse on the two sides. Return the sorted list.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def quicksort_list(values):
    def partition(arr, lo, hi):
        pivot = arr[hi]
        i = lo - 1
        for j in range(lo, hi):
            if arr[j] <= pivot:
                i += 1
                arr[i], arr[j] = arr[j], arr[i]
        arr[i + 1], arr[hi] = arr[hi], arr[i + 1]
        return i + 1

    def quicksort(arr, lo, hi):
        if lo < hi:
            p = partition(arr, lo, hi)
            quicksort(arr, lo, p - 1)
            quicksort(arr, p + 1, hi)

    a = values[:]
    quicksort(a, 0, len(a) - 1)
    return a


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = quicksort_list(values)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

def min_boats(people, limit):

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def reverse_groups(head, k):
    node = head
    count = 0
    while node is not None:
        count += 1
        node = node.next
    new_head = None
    prev_tail = None
    curr = head
    while count >= k:
        group_head = curr
        prev = None
        i = 0
        while i < k:
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
            i += 1
        if new_head is None:
            new_head = prev
        else:
            prev_tail.next = prev
        prev_tail = group_head
        count -= k
    if prev_tail is not None:
        prev_tail.next = curr
    if new_head is None:
        return head
    return new_head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    k = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_chain(values)
    head = reverse_groups(head, k)
    print(' '.join(map(str, chain_values(head))))


main()

questions.sourcecode:
from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def completion_order(bursts, quantum):
    q = deque(range(len(bursts)))
    left = list(bursts)
    done = []
    while q:
        i = q.popleft()
        step = left[i] if left[i] < quantum else quantum
        left[i] -= step
        if left[i] == 0:
            done.append(i)
        else:
            q.append(i)
    return done


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    quantum = int(lines[0].split()[1])
    bursts = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, completion_order(bursts, quantum))))


main()

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def turn_holder(head, k):
    node = head
    i = 0
    while i < k:
        node = node.next
        i += 1
    return node.value


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    k = int(data[1 + n])

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def dll_insert_at(head, pos, x):

head is the head Node of the chain. Insert Node(x) so it lands at 0-based position pos (inserting at pos = n appends after the tail) and return the (possibly new) head. The harness prints the chain forward AND backward to verify both directions.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of jobs.
Line 2: n integers — the job ids in chain order.
Line 3: the position pos (0 <= pos <= n).

Line 2: the chain backward, space-separated.

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def dll_insert_at(head, pos, x):
    node = Node(x)
    if pos == 0:
        node.next = head
        head.prev = node
        return node
    prev = head
    i = 0
    while i < pos - 1:
        prev = prev.next
        i += 1
    node.prev = prev
    node.next = prev.next
    if prev.next is not None:
        prev.next.prev = node
    prev.next = node
    return head


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    pos = int(data[1 + n])
    x = int(data[2 + n])
    head = build_dll_chain(values)
    head = dll_insert_at(head, pos, x)
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_forward(head))))
    print(' '.join(map(str, dll_backward(head))))


main()

questions.sourcecode:
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(300000)


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


class TNode:
    def __init__(self, v):
        self.val = v
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def build_tree(tokens):
    it = iter(tokens)
    first = next(it, -1)
    if first == -1:
        return None
    root = TNode(first)
    q = [root]
    for node in q:
        l = next(it, -1)
        if l != -1:
            node.left = TNode(l)
            q.append(node.left)
        r = next(it, -1)
        if r != -1:
            node.right = TNode(r)
            q.append(node.right)
    return root


def inorder(root, out):
    if root is None:
        return
    inorder(root.left, out)
    out.append(root.val)
    inorder(root.right, out)


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    root = build_tree(list(map(int, lines[1].split())))
    out = []
    inorder(root, out)
    print(' '.join(map(str, out)))


main()

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def merge_chains(head1, head2):
    dummy = Node(0)
    tail = dummy
    a, b = head1, head2
    while a is not None and b is not None:
        if a.value <= b.value:
            tail.next = a
            a = a.next
        else:
            tail.next = b
            b = b.next
        tail = tail.next
    if a is not None:
        tail.next = a
    else:
        tail.next = b
    return dummy.next


def main():

    n2 = int(data[1 + n1])

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


def build_dll_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        node.prev = tail
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def build_singly(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def tail_node(head):
    node = head
    while node.next is not None:
        node = node.next
    return node


def dll_forward(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out


def dll_backward(head):
    node = tail_node(head)
    out = []
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.prev
    return out


def build_circle(values):
    head = build_singly(values)
    tail = tail_node(head)
    tail.next = head
    return head


def circle_lap(head):
    out = [head.value]
    node = head.next
    while node is not head:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def split_circle(head):
    slow = head
    fast = head
    while fast.next is not head and fast.next.next is not head:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
    head2 = slow.next
    slow.next = head
    tail2 = head2
    while tail2.next is not head:
        tail2 = tail2.next
    tail2.next = head2

def main():

    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    head = build_circle(values)

import sys


def stable_order(pairs):
    a = pairs[:]
    for i in range(1, len(a)):
        cur = a[i]
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and a[j][0] > cur[0]:
            a[j + 1] = a[j]
            j -= 1
        a[j + 1] = cur
    return [p[1] for p in a]

import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def stock_spans(prices):
    n = len(prices)
    spans = [0] * n
    stack = []
    for i in range(n):
        while stack and prices[stack[-1]] <= prices[i]:
            stack.pop()
        spans[i] = i + 1 if not stack else i - stack[-1]
        stack.append(i)
    return spans


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    prices = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, stock_spans(prices))))


main()

import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def count_subarrays(nums, k):
    freq = {0: 1}
    total = 0
    ans = 0
    for x in nums:
        total += x
        ans += freq.get(total - k, 0)
        freq[total] = freq.get(total, 0) + 1
    return ans


def main():

import sys


def missing_number(batch):
    n = len(batch)
    acc = 0
    i = 0
    while i <= n:

        i += 1
    i = 0

    return acc

from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def diverted(cars, k):
    q = deque(cars)
    i = 0
    out = []
    while q:
        car = q.popleft()
        i += 1
        if i % k == 0:
            out.append(car)
    return out


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    k = int(lines[0].split()[1])
    cars = lines[1].split()
    print(' '.join(diverted(cars, k)))


main()

import sys


def tuples_by_second(pairs):
    a = pairs[:]
    n = len(a)
    for i in range(n):
        m = i
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if a[j][1] < a[m][1] or (a[j][1] == a[m][1] and a[j][0] < a[m][0]):
                m = j
        a[i], a[m] = a[m], a[i]
    return a


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    pairs = []
    idx = 1
    for _ in range(n):
        pairs.append((int(data[idx]), int(data[idx + 1])))
        idx += 2
    result = tuples_by_second(pairs)
    out = []
    for a, b in result:
        out.append(str(a) + ' ' + str(b))
    print('\n'.join(out))


main()

import sys


def two_sum_pair(values, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(values) - 1
    while lo < hi:
        s = values[lo] + values[hi]
        if s == target:
            return values[lo], values[hi]
        if s < target:
            lo += 1
        else:
            hi -= 1
    return -1, -1

import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def value_at(head, pos):
    node = head
    i = 0
    while i < pos:
        node = node.next
        i += 1
    return node.value


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    pos = int(data[1 + n])
    head = build_chain(values)
    print(value_at(head, pos))


main()

import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def warmer_days(temps):
    n = len(temps)
    res = [0] * n
    stack = []
    for i in range(n):
        while stack and temps[stack[-1]] < temps[i]:
            j = stack.pop()
            res[j] = i - j
        stack.append(i)
    return res


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    temps = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, warmer_days(temps))))


main()

questions.description:
A ticket chain has looped somewhere (or not at all). Extend Floyd's tortoise-and-hare: after slow and fast meet, restart one pointer at the head and step both one link at a time — they meet exactly at the loop's entry node.

The program scaffolding (input reading, Node class and chain building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def cycle_start(head):

head is the head Node of the chain; the harness has already linked the tail back to a node when the input says so. Return the VALUE of the node where the loop begins, or -1 when the chain is linear. Storing visited nodes is banned — the grader rejects set( and dict(.

Input Format:

Line 2: n integers — the node values in chain order.
Line 3: pos: the 0-based index the tail loops back to, or -1 when the chain is linear.

Output Format:
One line with the entry node's value, or -1.

Constraints:

questions.sourcecode:
import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


def build_chain(values):
    head = None
    tail = None
    for v in values:
        node = Node(v)
        if head is None:
            head = node
        else:
            tail.next = node
        tail = node
    return head


def chain_values(head):
    out = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    return out

def build_chain_with_cycle(values, pos):
    head = build_chain(values)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        steps = pos
        while steps > 0:
            target = target.next
            steps -= 1
        tail.next = target
    return head

def cycle_start(head):
    slow = head
    fast = head
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        if slow is fast:
            finder = head
            while finder is not slow:
                finder = finder.next
                slow = slow.next
            return finder.value
    return -1


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()

questions.description:

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def words_by_length_then_alpha(words):

Return the words ordered by (length, word) ascending: shorter words first; equal-length words in lexicographic (alphabetical) order. Use a manual sort with the compound comparison.

Input Format:

questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100; 1 <= len(word) <= 20; lowercase words, no spaces
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def words_by_length_then_alpha(words):
    a = words[:]
    for i in range(1, len(a)):
        cur = a[i]
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and (len(a[j]) > len(cur) or (len(a[j]) == len(cur) and a[j] > cur)):
            a[j + 1] = a[j]
            j -= 1
        a[j + 1] = cur
    return a


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    words = data[1:1 + n]
    result = words_by_length_then_alpha(words)
    print(' '.join(result))


main()
